source_title: MCG-NJU/AutoTavern: TavernGym and TavernBench: a faithful, full-content Hearthstone Battlegrounds simulator with an RL interface, and a 960-task decision benchmark. Code and data for "Build, Don't Play". - GitHub
source_excerpt:
A fast simulator and a decision benchmark for Hearthstone Battlegrounds.
Quick Start · TavernGym · TavernBench · Documentation · Citation
AutoTavern brings the decisions of Battlegrounds into a reproducible environment for AI research: simulate complete games, connect a learning algorithm, or evaluate a model's judgment against a fixed set of tasks.
This is the code and data release for Build, Don't Play: Self-Improving LLM Research Agents Develop a Hearthstone Battlegrounds AI That Rivals Top Players , by Changlian Ma and Limin Wang, Nanjing University and Shanghai AI Laboratory.
The release includes TavernGym and TavernBench. The trained TavernAgent, its weights and training code, and the benchmark item generators are not included.
Install with Python 3.10 or newer and a Rust toolchain . The version in rust-toolchain.toml is installed automatically by rustup.
This plays a full eight-player game with the included scripted bots. Replace a bot's action with your own legal action to control a seat.
This scores released answers against the labels. It needs only Python's standard library: no simulator build, model access or API key is required.
TavernGym reproduces solo Battlegrounds for client 36.6.3.253932 , server rules 36.6.3 . It exposes the player-visible state, an exact legal action mask, and seeded save and restore.
The learning interface provides 245 discrete actions, 3,227 numeric features and 124 card indices per observation. Rules and lobby settings can be configured explicitly.
Environment guide · Architecture · Implemented cards · Timewarp rules
TavernBench tests combat predictions, warband arrangements, target choices and turn plans with a shared prompt format and common scoring code.
The 368-task evaluation set is released alongside all 960 tasks . Saved simulator states cover the 30 play scenarios; the ten rule-execution scenarios need no state. The released answers include TavernAgent, ten language models, Jev, and five tool-use runs.
To evaluate your own model, install the optional runners from the repository root:
Benchmark guide · Task data · Released answers · Scoring code
For development, run pip install -e ".[test]" and pytest . The Rust crate also works on its own with cargo test --release .
